phases.title: Survival
phases.goal: Greet people, introduce yourself, and handle basic café and shop exchanges in French.
can: Pronounce the French alphabet, the accents (é, è, ê, ç) and the key nasal vowels (an, on, in, un)
Use greetings and politeness: bonjour, merci, s'il vous plaît, au revoir, and the vous/tu distinction
Conjugate être and avoir in the present and give your name, age and nationality
Count 0–69 and tell basic time (il est deux heures)
Recognize noun gender and the articles le/la/les and un/une/des
Ask a simple question three ways: intonation, est-ce que, and quel/où/combien
phases.daily: 10 min pronunciation drills (accents & nasal vowels), 10 min core vocab flashcards (greetings, numbers), 5 min conjugating être/avoir aloud.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.goal: Talk about your daily life, likes and plans in the present and near future.
can: Conjugate regular -er, -ir and -re verbs plus aller, faire, prendre, venir in the present
Master the negation ne … pas / jamais / plus / rien and the article change to de
Use the partitive du/de la/des to talk about food and quantities
Make adjectives agree in gender and number, including BAGS adjectives placed before the noun
Express the near future with aller + infinitive (je vais partir)
Count 70–1000 (soixante-dix, quatre-vingts, quatre-vingt-dix) and use days, months and dates
phases.daily: 15 min verb conjugation practice, 10 min listening to slow French dialogues, 10 min writing 3–4 sentences about your day.

phases.title: Core Structures
phases.goal: Narrate past events and handle real-life situations like travel, shopping and appointments.
can: Form the passé composé with avoir and with être (DR & MRS VANDERTRAMP verbs) with correct agreement
Use the imparfait for description and habits, and choose it vs the passé composé
Handle reflexive (pronominal) verbs: se lever, s'appeler, se coucher in present and past
Replace nouns with direct/indirect object pronouns (le/la/les, lui/leur) and with y and en
Give commands with the impératif (Parle ! Ne t'inquiète pas !)
Compare things with plus/moins/aussi … que and use the superlative le plus … de
phases.daily: 15 min passé composé vs imparfait exercises, 15 min reading a short news article or story, 10 min speaking practice describing a past event.

phases.title: Fluency
phases.goal: Express opinions, hypotheses and nuance, and hold longer conversations with confidence.
can: Use the futur simple with its irregular stems (ser-, aur-, ir-, fer-, viendr-)
Form and use the conditionnel for politeness and hypotheticals (je voudrais, si j'avais … je ferais)
Build the présent du subjonctif after il faut que, vouloir que, bien que and emotion verbs
Connect ideas with relative pronouns qui, que, dont and où
Master si-clauses: si + présent → futur, and si + imparfait → conditionnel
Follow and take part in native-speed conversations on familiar topics
phases.daily: 20 min watching French series with French subtitles, 15 min subjunctive and conditional drills, 15 min conversation or journaling with new connectors.

phases.title: Mastery
phases.goal: Communicate precisely and idiomatically across formal and informal registers, close to a native speaker.
can: Use the plus-que-parfait and the past conditional for the 'past-before-past' and unreal past (si j'avais su …)
Command adverb formation in -ment (-amment, -emment) and refined word order
Switch between registers: soutenu, courant and familiar, including dropping ne in speech
Recognize literary tenses (passé simple) when reading novels and formal texts
Handle idioms, faux amis and cultural nuance (ça marche, quand même, n'importe quoi)
Read newspapers, essays and literature and write structured, argued French texts
phases.daily: 30 min reading authentic literature or press, 15 min shadowing native audio for prosody, 15 min writing or debating a topic and self-correcting.
